item.title: How the La-5 Changed the Air War on the Eastern Front
item.description: The Lavochkin La-5 marked a turning point for Soviet fighter aviation during the Second World War. It was the first domestically produced fighter to reach rough parity with German aircraft on the Eastern Front, restoring confidence at a time when earlier designs consistently fell short. item.title: Fiat G.55 – Italy’s Centaur of WW2
item.description: In 1943, Italy found itself fighting to remain relevant in an air war that was rapidly leaving its earlier fighters behind. The Regia Aeronautica urgently needed a new generation interceptor capable of meeting Allied aircraft on equal terms. Three contenders emerged to answer that call: Fiat’s G.55 Centauro, Macchi’s M.C.205 Veltro, and Reggiane’s Re.2005 Sagittario.
